## Overview

This report investigates whether it is possible to predict whether a driver was injured in a road traffic collision when an injured front-seat passenger was also present. The analysis uses classification models fitted to road collision data derived from the [UK STATS19](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistical-data-sets/road-safety-open-data) database.

In this section, briefly describe:

- what is being predicted (driver injury)
- the type of data being used (road collision data)
- the purpose of the analysis
- the classification models fitted

You may wish to write a short paragraph similar to:

"This report investigates whether it is possible to predict whether a driver was injured in a road traffic collision when an injured front-seat passenger was also present. The analysis uses information describing the collision, vehicle and road environment to build classification models capable of estimating the probability of driver injury.

Do not describe implementation details, code, software, or the modelling pipeline in this section.

## The data

Describe the dataset used in your analysis.

The analysis is based on data from the UK STATS19 road safety statistics collection. The modelling dataset was created by combining information from multiple STATS19 tables describing:

- collisions
- vehicles involved in collisions
- casualties involved in collisions

These tables were joined together to create a single analysis dataset suitable for supervised learning.

The data were then restricted to:

- collisions involving an injured front-seat passenger

Each row in the final dataset represents a single driver involved in a qualifying collision.

## Variables

The coursework pipeline initially selects a small set of variables for analysis. At the time of writing these are:

- `driver_injured` (outcome variable)
- `sex_of_driver`
- `first_point_of_impact`
- `road_surface_conditions`
- `speed_limit`
- `road_type`
- `hour_of_day`

The outcome variable is driver_injured. All remaining variables are used as predictors.

The default variable selection is controlled by the `COLUMNS_TO_KEEP` list in:

`scripts/supervised/01_load_data_cw.py`

You are encouraged to experiment with alternative predictor variables if you believe they may improve model performance or provide additional insight. If you modify the variable selection, make regular commits to GitHub so that your work is version controlled and changes can be tracked.
